correctness.rationale: For each permitted affine Toeplitz-composition generator, the single-factor criterion is independently checked against its unique Gaussian symbol and the full source Corollary 3.1. Nonzero slope phases lie in (-pi/2,pi/2), with radii <= cos(phase); log cos is strictly concave. Jensen plus the angular winding lower bound gives the exact n-factor slope bound, and equality forces every generator slope onto the source boundary where intercepts vanish. Equal-slope affine factors explicitly realize all strict interior slopes with arbitrary translation and every centered endpoint. Monotonicity of x log cos(theta/x), with a positive derivative, gives the exact minimum and one-extra-factor penalty. The zero-slope and unimodular exclusions follow from nonzero permitted factors. Independent numerical diagnostics passed 79,629 finite assertions; no infinite claim relies on them.

value.rationale: The newly established one-symbol Toeplitz recognition condition defines a natural proper generating subset of Fock affine composition operators; the exact shortest restricted factorization is an intrinsic operator-semigroup invariant. The result completely classifies all n-factor reachable affine maps, proves rigid saturation, exhibits the discontinuous one-factor penalty for any nonzero translation at a sharp boundary, and determines the diverging factor cost near nonidentity rotations. This supplies global sharp structure, not an arbitrary finite example or a mere numerical threshold.
